plain_zero.label: Plain zero
plain_zero.reason: The dotted zero is the default. ss04 gives every glyph that carries the zero dot a copy without it, with the same outline and advance, so a plain zero can be chosen without changing any width.

italic.reason: Slanted 15 degrees about half the x-height: DIN 16's 75 degrees to the baseline. DINish Italic slants 12. DINish Italic keeps its operators and marks of the frame upright; DINDOT adds its arrows, mathematics, geometric and status symbols, the service mark and sound recording copyright beside the copyright, registered and trademark signs, and the superscript and subscript plus, minus and equals. Everything else slants, with each stroke kept at its upright thickness, its corners rounded again as circles and its dots kept round. Bowls are balanced inside the stroke correction: in every corner the outer side of a curve takes 2 - cs of the correction and the inner side cs, with 3% more stroke in the acute corners and 3% less in the obtuse ones; cs is searched per bowl until its counter's obtuse/acute corner ratio is 1.5 times the upright's (the plain shear gives about 1.85). Where tangent pieces end apart, the difference is tapered in over one stroke width.
